messages:
elaine: Need a crisp split for operator vs control-plane responsibilities for dedicated GPU pool autoscaling. Quick ideas?
tom: Operator = node health, local prewarm state, immediate admission check; emits raw primitives. Control plane = global policy, banking, headroom math.
priya: Agree. Operator should provide a synchronous admit API that returns allowed/lane/est_warmup_ms. Example response: {allowed:true,lane:"prewarm",est_ms:2500}.
marco: Telemetry minimal set: gpu_free_slots (gauge), prewarm_reserved (gauge), warmup_inflight (gauge), model_load_failures_total (counter), fallback_count_total (counter), warmup_p95_ms (gauge). Emit at 10s cadence, push events on failures.
elaine: Label set: pool_id, model_family, zone, operator_version. No tenant ids; use hashed_tenant_bucket for spike detection.
tom: Operator should aggregate 10s and 1m windows locally and export summaries to reduce traffic, but keep raw events locally for 48h.
priya: Control plane computes headroom_deficit_1m/5m, fallback_rate_5m, tenant_spike_buckets. Alert if fallback_rate_5m > 0.5% for SLA tenants.
marco: Telemetry event format suggestion: {ts:7720000000,pool_id:"pool-a",event:"model_load_start",model:"mixtral-8x",schema_v:1}. Include schema_v.
ops-bot: auto: created follow-up doc: "autoscale-signal-split" in /docs (owner=elaine).
elaine: Action items: I will draft the admit API proto; tom will add aggregation pseudo; priya will propose alert thresholds. Sync tomorrow 30m.
